tasks.short: Negotiate event supplier prices, service commitments and contract terms.

steps.what: Collect supplier proposals and identify prices, exclusions, cancellation terms and service commitments.

loop.output: Structured terms with source passages and missing-field flags.
loop.check: Validate currencies, dates and totals; link each extracted term to its source.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per proposal; unresolved fields go to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier documents express exclusions and cancellation terms in varied prose.

steps.what: Compare total costs, minimum commitments and cancellation exposure.
Agree spending limits, acceptable concessions and terms requiring escalation.
Negotiate price, service details and concessions with the supplier.
Update the contract draft to reflect negotiated terms.

loop.input: Supplier contract draft, negotiated terms and approved clauses.
loop.check: Show every change; verify prices and dates; flag departures from approved clauses.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; ambiguous agreements remain unresolved for human review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier clauses differ, and negotiated language must be mapped into existing wording.

steps.what: Review liability, cancellation and nonstandard clauses; clear or escalate exceptions.
Approve the commitment, sign and file the final contract.

tasks.design: An event record in the {WORKFLOW} links proposals, budget limits and negotiation mandates; deterministic calculations produce the supplier comparison. Bounded extraction and drafting loops prepare source-linked summaries and redlines in the {DOCS}, while people negotiate and clear exceptions. Configured approvals in the {ESIGN} and filing in the {CLM} control the final commitment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier terms vary, and negotiated changes arrive through conversations and attachments. Building the comparison and approval connections often cost more than recurring events justified.
tasks.enabler_now: Configuration and AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building reusable comparisons and approval flows. Bounded text extraction can prepare summaries without negotiating or making commitments.
tasks.still_hard: Commercial leverage, supplier trust and liability trade-offs remain human work. Confidential terms need controlled access, and poor source documents still require clarification.
tasks.human_edge: Read the supplier's priorities, trade concessions and recognise when a cheap offer creates delivery risk.

ambition.what: A reusable cancellation-exposure review for each event portfolio.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time assembling terms and more time preparing negotiation positions. They can propose portfolio-level cancellation limits; spending and signature authority remain with existing approvers.

reach.task: Choose which event commitments to retain when the marketing budget changes.
reach.learn: Campaign priorities, sunk costs and the value of alternative uses of the budget.

evidence.claim: Structured cost comparisons, approval routing and contract filing are feasible with deterministic rules and configuration.
Pactum documents purchasing policy checks inside Coupa; this supports adjacent procurement feasibility, not autonomous event negotiation.
Event-specific extraction quality, time reductions and build ranges are estimates requiring a pilot.

assumptions: The planner negotiates within a spending mandate rather than holding unrestricted signature authority.
The typical process mixes proposal emails, cost workbooks, negotiation calls and contract documents.
Legal review is concentrated on exceptions; standard agreements use an approved checklist.
The first build supports one contract family and uses reusable schemas rather than company-specific negotiation logic.
unknowns: Available configuration and export access in the {CLM}, {PROCUREMENT} and {ESIGN}.
Actual signature limits and legal-review thresholds.
Volume, languages and consistency of supplier contracts.
Whether contractual restrictions allow proposal processing through the chosen model service.
research_questions: Which contract fields can be extracted reliably from representative supplier documents?
Can existing approval configuration cover the commitment controls without custom code?
Which cost and cancellation scenarios recur enough to justify reusable calculators?
new_work: Review extracted terms and contract redlines.
Resolve ambiguous agreements and missing supplier information.
Maintain clause templates, approval limits and calculation rules.
Monitor access, connector failures and contract-version mismatches.

tasks.short: Evaluate event suppliers against requirements and select the provider.

steps.what: Confirm event needs, mandatory conditions and acceptable trade-offs with the event sponsor.
Send requirements to potential suppliers and request comparable proposals.
Read proposals and record capacity, availability, inclusions and requirement gaps.

loop.input: Supplier proposals and a fixed requirement schema.
loop.output: Source-linked supplier facts and unanswered requirements.
loop.check: Validate dates, capacities and amounts; distinguish explicit claims from absent information.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per proposal; missing facts require supplier clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposals use varied prose and document layouts rather than a common data format.

steps.what: Build a comparison of cost, mandatory requirements and unresolved gaps.
Inspect shortlisted services or venues and test delivery claims with suppliers.
Choose the provider after weighing fit, delivery risk and budget.
Record the approved selection and its rationale for contracting.

tasks.design: A configured intake in the {WORKFLOW} sends approved proposal requests and collects comparable supplier facts. A bounded extraction loop reads attachments from the {DOCS}; deterministic checks create a comparison with explicit gaps rather than treating missing information as failure. People assess delivery quality and approve selection, then the {PROCUREMENT} receives the decision and its rationale.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier facts were scattered across proposals, messages and visits. Existing purchasing records rarely captured the event-specific requirements needed for a useful comparison.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable intake forms and inexpensive comparison code can organise the structured facts. Bounded extraction can reduce re-entry from proposals while retaining source passages.
tasks.still_hard: Venue suitability, service quality and contingency readiness cannot be established from supplier claims alone. Availability changes quickly, and subjective weights can hide important trade-offs.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a supplier can deliver this event and challenge reassuring claims with practical questions.

ambition.what: A backup-provider readiness review for critical event services.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time copying proposal details and more time testing supplier readiness. They can recommend a backup-provider threshold; final supplier and spending decisions stay with the budget owner.

reach.task: Assess the environmental implications of venue and service choices.
reach.learn: Evidence requirements, comparable activity measures and limits of supplier sustainability claims.

evidence.claim: Forms, requirement checks and comparable cost calculations can use configuration and deterministic code.
Source-linked proposal extraction is plausible, but the digest provides no event-supplier selection case.
The proposed time shares and build ranges are planning estimates rather than measured customer results.

assumptions: Several providers are considered for material services; routine repeat purchases may use a shorter process.
The planner maintains a workbook because event requirements do not fit the purchasing record well.
Cost and mandatory conditions are structured; service quality remains a human assessment.
The shortlist is provisional, and unknown facts do not automatically exclude a supplier.
unknowns: Which event services require competition or procurement involvement.
Whether an existing {PROCUREMENT} comparison module covers the requirements.
Availability of supplier performance records and permission to reuse them.
Actual approval roles and the importance of venue visits.
research_questions: Which requirement fields recur across venues, caterers, speakers and technical suppliers?
Can supplier intake replace enough attachment extraction to remove the model loop?
Which comparison flags help assess risk without creating false certainty?
new_work: Verify extracted facts and obtain missing supplier answers.
Maintain requirement templates and comparable cost definitions.
Refresh availability and remove stale supplier information.
Check that comparison weights and flags do not obscure critical requirements.

tasks.short: Develop the event programme, agenda, budget and delivery plan with the event sponsor.

steps.what: Discuss objectives, audience needs, format and success measures with the event sponsor.
Consolidate requirements, constraints and stakeholder amendments into an event brief.

loop.output: Structured brief, constraints and unresolved conflicts.
loop.check: Link requirements to sources; flag conflicting dates, budgets and audience assumptions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; conflicts go to the planner without inferred resolution.
loop.why_not_simpler: Stakeholders express constraints and amendments in free text.

steps.what: Draft the programme, session sequence and agenda.

loop.input: Event brief, approved programme templates and confirmed speaker availability.
loop.output: Agenda draft with timing and unresolved content needs.
loop.check: Check durations, breaks, speaker availability and coverage of stated objectives.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision after planner comments; remaining conflicts return to manual planning.
loop.why_not_simpler: Session descriptions and sequencing require interpretation of audience needs and event objectives.

steps.what: Calculate the budget, contingency and attendance-dependent cost scenarios.
Map services, owners, deadlines and dependencies into a delivery schedule.
Resolve programme and service trade-offs with the event sponsor.
Approve the programme, service scope, budget and delivery commitments.
Distribute the approved plan and relevant instructions to delivery teams and suppliers.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} maintains a structured event brief, while bounded loops prepare source-linked requirements and an agenda draft in the {DOCS}. Deterministic calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} produce budget scenarios, and configured templates in the {PROJECT} create delivery schedules. People resolve trade-offs and approve commitments before the {EMAIL} sends audience-specific briefings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements, agendas, budgets and delivery schedules were separate artefacts that changed together. Keeping them connected required custom work, while programme quality still depended on understanding the audience.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting a reusable event schema to calculators and schedule templates. Bounded drafting can prepare an editable starting point from approved material.
tasks.still_hard: A coherent programme needs editorial judgement, speaker cooperation and realistic delivery assumptions. GDPR applies to attendee data; accessibility and venue requirements need local verification, and AI Act obligations depend on the use.
tasks.human_edge: Choose an event experience that serves the audience and resolve competing sponsor priorities.

ambition.what: A weekly attendance-triggered decision on service scope and contingency spending.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time keeping documents and budgets aligned and more time comparing programme choices. They can receive delegated authority to adjust approved service quantities within defined thresholds; larger changes still require the budget owner.

reach.task: Turn audience research into event objectives and evaluation questions.
reach.learn: Sampling, survey design and how to distinguish attendance from meaningful audience outcomes.

reach.task: Shape session descriptions and the programme's narrative.
reach.learn: Audience-focused structure, editorial standards and speaker brief development.

evidence.claim: Budget calculations, dependency templates and document generation are suitable for deterministic implementation.
Bounded drafting from approved sources can prepare agenda alternatives, but the digest contains no documented event-planning case.
The proposed weekly decision cadence and build ranges depend on data freshness and existing access.

assumptions: The company has a repeatable event programme rather than only occasional one-off events.
The planner uses documents for agendas, a workbook for budget scenarios and the {PROJECT} for delivery coordination.
A shared event schema can serve multiple employers through configurable templates and field mappings.
Build estimates cover a pilot with one event format and existing authorised infrastructure.
The time split gives meetings substantial weight, while recognising that budget and document preparation are separable.
unknowns: Existing planning templates and available configuration in the {PROJECT}.
Where registrations and current attendance forecasts are held.
Which supplier costs change with attendance and their change deadlines.
Whether the planner can receive delegated authority over service quantities.
Whether attendee processing or employee participation requires additional consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which event formats share enough constraints to use one planning schema?
Which agenda drafts improve planning quality rather than merely producing more text?
How should budget scenarios handle uncertain attendance and supplier change deadlines?
new_work: Review brief extraction and agenda drafts.
Maintain programme templates, cost assumptions and delivery dependencies.
Check budget freshness and manage approved-plan versions.
Verify recipients and confidential content before external briefings.

tasks.short: Recruit, prepare, schedule and supervise event support staff and volunteers.

steps.what: Define support roles, headcount, required skills and shift coverage.
Publish approved role requests and organise applications or expressions of interest.
Interview candidates or volunteers and decide who fits each role.
Prepare employment or volunteer engagement terms from approved templates.
Approve engagement terms and obtain required signatures.
Collect availability, relevant qualifications and support needs from confirmed staff.
Assign shifts and roles, check coverage and confirm the roster.
Prepare role-specific induction packs, job cards and escalation contacts.
Train staff, practise procedures and check understanding.
Record completed training and outstanding requirements.
Supervise live work, handle welfare concerns and redirect staff as conditions change.

tasks.design: Configure recruitment administration in the {ATS} and volunteer records in the {WORKFLOW}, with template engagement documents routed through the {ESIGN}. Structured availability feeds deterministic coverage checks and a proposed roster; approved role content generates induction packs in the {DOCS}, and completion records feed the {LMS} or the {PROJECT}. People select staff, approve engagements and rosters, deliver practical training and supervise the event.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paid staff, volunteers and temporary support followed different record paths. Availability, induction and roster updates often depended on manual coordination across those paths.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing form, template and approval features can handle much of the administration. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting availability, roster checks and training records without adding candidate scoring.
tasks.still_hard: Selection, practical competence, welfare and live supervision remain human responsibilities. GDPR applies to staff data; support needs may reveal sensitive information, and national rules govern employment and employee consultation. Hiring or worker-evaluation AI would need separate EU AI Act assessment [S17]; it is outside this design.
tasks.human_edge: Build confidence, recognise unsafe or unsuitable assignments and respond fairly when people struggle.

ambition.what: A supported first-event pathway for inexperienced volunteers.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time chasing availability and preparing repeated paperwork, leaving more time for coaching and safe deployment. They can propose a buddy-based volunteer pathway; hiring, employment terms and staffing-budget authority stay with their existing owners.

reach.task: Prepare front-of-house staff to handle sensitive attendee questions.
reach.learn: Approved messaging, escalation routes and practical communication rehearsal.

reach.task: Write clear role instructions and emergency job cards.
reach.learn: Task-based instructions, plain language and testing documents with inexperienced users.

evidence.claim: Recruitment administration, availability forms, template documents and completion recording can use existing configuration.
Deterministic roster checks can test availability, qualification requirements, overlap and coverage without evaluating worker performance.
The proposed gains and consultation ranges are estimates; the digest contains no event-staffing implementation case.

assumptions: The representative event uses a mix of temporary paid support and volunteers; internal-only events omit recruitment and engagement steps.
Paid applications use the {ATS}; volunteer expressions of interest use the {PROJECT} or equivalent configured records.
Paid training completions use the {LMS}; volunteer completions may remain in the {PROJECT}.
A rules-based roster proposes assignments from declared availability and explicit requirements, without candidate ranking or inferred personal traits.
The consultation range includes access approval and employee consultation under national rules where applicable; formal procedures may take longer.
unknowns: Actual staffing mix, engagement categories and responsibility for volunteer administration.
Existing availability, scheduling and training configuration.
Applicable national rules, collective agreements and employee-representative consultation requirements.
Which support needs must be collected and who may access them.
Whether cross-system configuration can record confirmed engagements and training without custom connectors.
research_questions: Can existing scheduling configuration satisfy coverage rules before custom code is considered?
Which practical training checks must remain trainer-confirmed rather than recorded as attendance alone?
How can volunteer records remain useful without collecting unnecessary personnel data?
Which induction modules enable inexperienced volunteers to work safely with a buddy?
new_work: Review proposed staffing levels, rosters and induction packs.
Handle availability conflicts, missing qualifications and late withdrawals.
Maintain role requirements, training content and scheduling rules.
Correct failed record transfers and verify training-completion evidence.
Manage personnel-data access, retention and applicable consultation.

role.altitude: The planner's week shifts from assembling information and chasing updates toward programme choices, supplier readiness and staff coaching. Decision rights can expand to approved service adjustments and staffing deployment within explicit limits; supplier commitments and employment decisions retain named approvers.
reach: Marketing managers: connect event scope and commitments to campaign priorities.
Market research analysts: define audience outcomes and useful evaluation questions.
Sustainability specialists: compare venue and service impacts using defensible evidence.
Editors and technical writers: improve programme narratives and practical staff instructions.
Public relations specialists: prepare staff for sensitive attendee interactions.
skills_to_grow: Structure event requirements and distinguish confirmed facts from assumptions.
Build and interpret cost, attendance and cancellation scenarios.
Test supplier delivery claims and prepare negotiation positions.
Review source-linked extraction and drafts efficiently.
Design safe staffing coverage, practical training and volunteer support.
Maintain access, approval and data-quality rules across connected records.
role.ambitious_version: Run a repeatable event-readiness service that joins programme quality, supplier contingencies, budget exposure and staff preparation. Offer smaller internal teams a guided planning path, with clear escalation points for commitments and live delivery risks.
